html:
Austria-Hungary was the empire of the Habsburgs in Central Europe from 1867 to 1918: two largely self-governing states, Austria and Hungary, sharing one monarch, one army and one foreign policy. It is shown here in 1880 and 1900.

It was born from defeat. After losing to Prussia in the Austro-Prussian War of 1866, the Austrian Empire made the Compromise of 1867 with the Hungarian nobility. Franz Joseph was emperor in Vienna and king in Budapest, and reigned through the whole period until 1916.

It held a dozen peoples: Germans, Hungarians, Czechs, Slovaks, Poles, Ukrainians, Romanians, Croats, Serbs, Slovenes and Italians. Their demands for rights and language filled its politics. Its cities boomed, and Vienna around 1900 was a centre of music, art, medicine and philosophy. In 1878 it took over Bosnia-Herzegovina, a step that later pulled it into conflict with Serbia and into the First World War, which destroyed it.
